name: reference
_comment: Reference solution for Round 2. Not the only good answer.
Nothing is blocked for being an agent. After Amazon v. Perplexity (9th Cir. 2026) a
user's local agent is the user, so the policy treats 'agent' as a client type, not a
verdict, and puts the weight where the farm differs from the shopper: reused
fingerprints, brand-new accounts, order velocity per account, and the absence of a
human at the money step. Undeclared agents are challenged, not blocked (declare or
pay a proof of work). Signed agents and assistive agents are capped at a challenge;
no_pointer alone is not exempted because at weight 5 it never blocks anyone by itself.
Checkout steps up to a human confirmation, which an unattended farm cannot answer
and a shopper's agent hands back to the shopper. Terms are clickwrap with a declared-
agent path, so there is a contract to point at. Appeal path on, 90-day logs.
